summary: An ordered, plain-language log of what the agent is doing. Status is text and shape, never colour alone.
useWhen: a run takes long enough that the user needs to know where it has got to
a person will decide whether to let it continue — which means they need to read what it did

useInstead.when: the output is prose rather than steps
you need a decision, not a report

composition.note: An <ol>, so a screen reader can say "3 of 7" and the order is structural rather than typed into each row.

guarantees: every step renders its status as visually hidden text as well as a glyph, and the glyphs differ in shape rather than only in colour — a row of coloured dots fails WCAG 1.4.1 outright
the active step is announced once, when it changes, in a polite live region
the active step's spinner stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`
requires: step text in the user's language — "Searched the invoice archive", not a function signature
`announceActive={false}` when several logs are on screen, or they narrate over each other
notes: The active step is read out of the children rather than taken as a prop. Two sources for one fact is how they come to disagree.

antiPatterns.dont: raw tool calls or JSON as the step label
antiPatterns.why: this is the account a person reads to decide whether to let the run continue
the announcement names one thing, and two claims about what is happening now cannot both be true

antiPatterns.dont: several announcing logs on one screen
antiPatterns.why: they interrupt each other and the user turns the whole thing off
